answer.text: Systematic realization of investments, settlement of liabilities, and distribution per the waterfall
Transferring all investments to another fund
Converting the AIF into a mutual fund

explanation.text: The Logic: On winding up (workbook p.220), the AIF's assets are liquidated and the proceeds are first applied to satisfy all liabilities of the scheme; only the net surplus is then distributed to investors. The order in which those proceeds reach investors follows the distribution waterfall described on pp.55-57, which sets out the priority of payments for fund proceeds. The Trap: Winding up is not merely an administrative closure (closing a bank account), nor is it a transfer of investments to another vehicle or a conversion into a mutual fund. It is a defined liquidation-and-distribution process governed by the fund documents and AIF Regulations. Note: Source references: NISM Series XIX-A workbook pp.55-57 (distribution waterfall / priority of payments) and p.220 (liquidation of assets, satisfaction of liabilities, and distribution on winding up).
